ai_analysis.summary: This promotional post announces a PDF about using SQL CASE WHEN for real-time customer segmentation and SQL interview preparation. It claims that placing business logic in SQL can reduce compute, improve dashboard load times, simplify pipelines, and centralize logic across ETL, BI, and analytics. It also mentions a telco segmentation example involving 20 million users and daily SQL logic. The PDF itself is not included, so no syntax, query implementation, optimization technique, or segmentation rule is provided.
subtopics: SQL-based segmentation for millions of users
Daily segmentation in a telco example
Compute reduction through SQL-based business logic

interview_questions.question: What real-world use case does the post associate with SQL CASE WHEN?
interview_questions.answer:
The use case is customer segmentation in real-time analytics.
The post says the approach can support segmentation for millions of users.
The referenced telco example contains 20 million users and uses daily segmentation logic.

interview_questions.question: What benefits does the post claim come from placing business logic in SQL?
interview_questions.answer:
The claimed benefits include lower compute requirements and faster dashboard loading.
Implementing the logic in SQL can reduce pipeline complexity.
SQL can hold shared business logic across ETL, BI, and analytics workflows.

interview_questions.question: Why does the post frame CASE WHEN as a strategy rather than only SQL syntax?
interview_questions.answer:
The post uses CASE WHEN to place business rules for customer segmentation directly in SQL.
Centralizing those rules is presented as a way to create cleaner and more audit-friendly pipelines.
The post contrasts memorizing CASE WHEN syntax with understanding its role in implementing analytics logic.
